Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

(CNN) -- The fourth and final suspect in the fatal shooting of two Arkansas university students turned himself in Monday, University of Central Arkansas police said. The first suspect was apprehended while driving about three minutes after the Sunday night shooting. The others were detained later, said Lt. Preston Grumbles. The suspects were identified as Kawin Brockton, 19; Kelsey Perry, 19; Mario Toney, 20 and Brandon Wade, 20. Police released little details on the suspects other than the fact that they were not university students. "It does not seem at this time that it was a random act," he said, but police are "unsure of the precise motive." He said there was "no indication" the shooting was gang-related. University police released the names of the victims Monday. Ryan Henderson, 18, of Little Rock, Arkansas, and Chavares Block, 19, of Dermott, Arkansas, were killed. Block was a sophomore pre-engineering major. Henderson was a freshman who had not yet declared a major. The university's student government will hold a candlelight vigil in memory of the students at 5 p.m. (6 p.m. ET) Monday. Religious organizations on campus will host a prayer vigil Tuesday. A third victim, Martrevis Norman, was treated at a hospital and released. He is not a student at the university, said Lt. Rhonda Swindle of UCA campus police. A hospital representative earlier told CNN that the survivor was shot in the leg. "This is something you pray never happens," interim university president Tom Courtway said, visibly upset. "But it happened." The shooting, which happened outside a dorm, prompted a campus lockdown and the cancellation of Monday classes. Courtway said classes will resume Tuesday.  Watch police describe the shooting » . The shots were fired near Arkansas Hall and the Snow Fine Arts Center at 9:22 p.m., Swindle said. Freshman Sam Hausen, who was about 50 feet (15 meters) away from the shooters when the gunfire began, said, "I heard about five or 10 shots and, at first, I thought it was just firecrackers, because everybody always clowns around out there, but I just realized that it wasn't firecrackers." As he began running away, he saw one of the wounded students hit the ground and another stumble into the dorm, he said. "I saw a couple cars speed off," Hausen said. "I don't know if they were the shooters or not." Student Lauren Knight, who was walking to the library when the shooting started, said students scurried for safety. When the campus lockdown was ordered, Knight was stuck with other students for several hours inside the library, she said. The university serves about 12,500 full-time students in Conway.

The gunfire erupted Sunday night outside Arkansas Hall on the university’s campus in Conway, about 30 miles northwest of Little Rock. University police said officers responding to reports of shots found multiple victims at the scene.

The dead were identified as 18-year-old UCA freshman Ryan Henderson and 19-year-old Chavares Block. Authorities have said Block was not enrolled at the university, although initial reports described both victims as students. A third person was treated for a gunshot wound.

Four men were taken into custody as investigators worked to determine what prompted the shooting. Police said the incident did not appear to be random, and there was no indication of an ongoing threat to the campus.

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the University of Central Arkansas campus shooting, including the victims, suspects, police statements, eyewitness accounts, vigils, and campus response.
counterfactuals.output:
### University of Central Arkansas campus shooting

On the night of **October 26, 2008**, gunfire erupted outside **Arkansas Hall**, a residence hall at the University of Central Arkansas in Conway. The shooting killed two young men and wounded a third.

- **Ryan Henderson**, 18, a UCA freshman from Little Rock, was killed.
- **Chavares Block Jr.**, 19, who was visiting campus and was not a UCA student, was also killed.
- **Martrevis Norman**, a UCA student, was wounded but survived.

### Suspects and police account

Police quickly arrested **Brandon Wade**, 20, and **Dejuan Moore**, 19, and pursued additional alleged participants. The suspects were described as nonstudents. Wade and Moore faced capital-murder and related charges; subsequent court proceedings produced convictions and lengthy prison sentences.

Investigators said the attack was **not believed to be a random mass shooting**. Police linked it to a dispute involving people who had come onto campus, while indicating that Henderson appeared to have been an unintended victim. Officers recovered evidence from the scene and interviewed numerous students and witnesses. UCA Police Chief **Larry James** and other authorities emphasized that the immediate threat had ended once suspects were identified and taken into custody.

### Eyewitness accounts

Students living near Arkansas Hall reported hearing a rapid series of shots—some initially mistook the noise for firecrackers—followed by screaming and people running for cover. Witnesses described seeing victims on the ground near the residence hall and students trying to help before police and emergency crews arrived. Residents were told to remain indoors while officers searched the campus and secured the area.

### Vigils and mourning

Hundreds of students, faculty members, friends, and relatives gathered for candlelight vigils and memorial events. Speakers remembered Henderson as a promising first-year student and expressed grief for both families. Participants prayed, observed moments of silence, and called for unity and an end to violence.

### Campus response

UCA issued emergency alerts, locked down affected areas, and **canceled classes the following day**. Counseling and grief-support services were made available, residence-hall staff met with students, and university officials increased police visibility while reviewing campus security and emergency-notification procedures. Administrators stressed that the violence involved visitors rather than an ongoing threat from within the student body, while acknowledging that the shooting deeply shook the campus community.
